assumptions: Agent learning processes are dominated by locally-linear updates.
Initial parameter noise impacts the specific convergence path but can be constrained.
Stability is measurable through distribution variance across independent runs with varying seeds.
definition.falsification: Preference variance remains high (>=0.5) even when initialization is constrained to small hyper-volumes, suggesting fundamental sensitivity to initial conditions.
definition.statement: Agents trained with locally-linear learning formulations exhibit bounded variance in preference convergence when initialized within a constrained hyper-volume of parameter space, distinct from global convergence.
definition.uncertainty: The definition of the constrained parameter hyper-volume is heuristic; true convergence bounds across non-linear subspaces are unknown.

definition.method: Execute a set of learning trials with randomized Gaussian initializations centered on different means to test variance across clusters.
definition.source:
import random
def experiment(inputs):
    trials = inputs.get('trials', 50)
    seeds = inputs.get('seeds', range(trials))
    results = []
    for seed in seeds:
        random.seed(seed)
        # Simulate learning trace as a sequence of locally-linear updates
        trace = [random.gauss(0.1, 0.05) for _ in range(50)]
        results.append(sum(trace[-10:]) / 10)
    return {'measurements': {'final_preference': results}}
definition.stop: Variance is consistently above 0.2 across three consecutive seed batches.
